editorial:
Imagine being an 11-year-old girl who feels completely lost after her parents split up. That is where you find Simone, a quiet kid who is trying to deal with a mother who struggles with drinking and sadness. You will feel the heavy mood right away as Simone tries to find a way to make her mom love her again. She creates a strange, mysterious world that feels more like a trap than a game. The movie keeps you guessing about what is real and what is just in her head, making you wonder if this little girl is actually dangerous or just lonely.

What really works here is how the movie builds tension without using cheap scares. The acting feels natural, and the twists keep you on your toes until the very end. It might feel a bit slow in the middle, but the payoff is worth it for fans of psychological mysteries.
endingExplained: At the end, you discover that the labyrinth is actually a way for Simone to control her mother. The twist reveals that Simone has been manipulating her environment to force her mother to focus only on her. It turns out the boundary she crossed was more than just a game; it was a mental trap. The movie ends with a chilling feeling that the mother might never truly escape her daughter's grip.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and creepy family stories.
